thread:
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started: sdk-0.16 -> feature: async_paging=true (canary 5%) at 2027-04-??T12:00:34Z
Alice: seeing spike in 502s on /v1/stream and paging endpoints around 12:03. paging iterator failing w/ handshake error. rolling canary? :grimacing:
Ben: oncall here, linking graphs. errors up 18% on generation and 35% on paged_list endpoints. is this client-side parsing? anyone on the runtime team? @Carmen
monitor-bot: Alert: paging-iterator-errors > threshold (18m) | affected hosts: r-infer-*-pool | p50 latency +120ms | error sample: "handshake: invalid frame: expected KV-INIT"
Carmen: I pushed async paging changes in 0.16 to improve throughput. quick read: client switches to streaming-first handshake header: `X-Redwood-Stream: async` and server must accept fallback. looks like older downstream proxies/clients are rejecting the handshake and returning 502.
Alice: snippet from logs: ```[12:03:12] WARN io.redwood.stream.Handshake - unexpected handshake frame from 10.2.4.15: "INVALID_HEADER: X-Redwood-Stream"
[12:03:12] ERROR pipeline - write failed: Broken pipe
```
Ben: customer impact? Maya? any tickets?
Maya (Customer Success): two paid customers opened P1s: AcmeMaps and FinPortal reporting streaming timeouts and partial results on paged queries. Both on Hosted tier, one on Dedicated (FinPortal). Support flagged elevated errors to them.
Jordan (Oncall-SRE): this looks like a compatibility regression. mitigation path: 1) flip feature-flag kill for async_paging 2) rollback canary if kill doesn't cut it 3) patch handshake fallback in runtime. Recommend immediate kill-switch.
Alice: applying kill-switch now -> toggling `sdk_async_paging` to false for prod canary pools.
deploy-bot: Feature flag `sdk_async_paging` toggled OFF for canary pools by Alice at 12:07:03Z
Ben: monitoring... error rate falling but still noisy. p95 latency normalizing.
monitor-bot: paging-iterator-errors down to baseline (5m) | p50 latency back to normal
Carmen: good catch. this confirms handshake incompat with some infra paths. I'll open a hotfix branch to add header-negotiation fallback and bind tests for older clients (0.14/0.15).
Maya (Customer Success): notified AcmeMaps and FinPortal: interim mitigation applied (feature flag off), working with eng on timeline for fix. Both acknowledged.
Alice: canary rollback queued: abort remaining 0.16 canaries and lock new rollouts until patch merges. kicking rollback now.
deploy-bot: Canary aborted: sdk-0.16 (canary 5%) by Alice at 12:12:47Z. Rollout frozen: tag=canary/freeze/sdk-0.16
Ben: assign postmortem owner and severity. I suggest Sev2 (customer-visible but mitigated). Carmen, can you own the postmortem and remediation?
Carmen: will own. initial notes: root cause = SDK 0.16 changed streaming handshake header without server-side backward compatibility; secondary cause = lack of canary path verification for proxies and dedicated networking. remediation items: handshake fallback in runtime, compatibility tests in CI, add canary smoke checks for paging endpoints.
Jordan (Oncall-SRE): handoff: I'm going offline at 12:30 UTC, leaving Ben as follow-up. Ben please escalate to infra if any Dedicated customers still impacted.
Ben: noted. I'll follow up with FinPortal SLA owner and prepare a customer summary.
Maya (Customer Success): draft message to customers ready, will send updated note once we have ETA for fix.
Carmen: estimated patch and canary re-release in ~3-6 hours depending on QA. will prioritize.
Alice: creating incident ticket in tracker and adding action items.
Ben: OK closing incident thread here once docs are in tracker. please add logs/metrics slices: timeframe 12:00-12:20 UTC, hosts r-infer-*pool, client_versions seen: 0.14,0.15,0.16.
Carmen: will attach failing handshake trace and test PR link to the ticket.
Maya (Customer Success): customers updated.
Ben: handing off to next oncall: @Jordan (oncall tomorrow) for followups. If anything flares, reopen thread. /incident close :white_check_mark:
notes: post-incident: rollback + feature-flag kill applied; customers notified; remediation assigned to Carmen; follow-up ticket created
